_comment: Scale-existence battery, oracle tier. One fixed 150-word source report (Halvorsen Desalination Plant) carrying 14 atomic facts (location; opening date; build cost; daily output; demand share; chief engineer; 2023 fouling incident and its 60% output cut; algal-bloom cause; fertilizer-runoff origin; repair duration; repair cost; UV pretreatment addition; weekly-to-monthly cleaning change; second plant approved for 2027). Each item = SOURCE + a ~50-word summary with a planted number of semantic errors (wrong numbers, swapped entities, fabricated additions, causal inversions); all summaries equally fluent, errors never grammatical. truth = 1 - errors/14; item id encodes the planted count (e0a/e0b perfect ... e8). Items descending by truth. Harmonic block: four summaries with exactly 2 errors each but of DIFFERENT species (numeric distortion x2, entity swap x2, fabricated addition x2, causal inversion x2) - identical truth, genuinely hard chordless-cycle comparisons.

attribute.primary: how faithful the summary is to its source: the degree to which every claim it makes is supported by the source text
attribute.opposite: how unfaithful the summary is to its source: how many of its claims distort or contradict the source text
paraphrases: the accuracy of its claims relative to the source
how well its statements are grounded in the source passage
its freedom from distortions of the source

SOURCE:
The Halvorsen Desalination Plant in Port Merrow opened in March 2019 after a construction program that cost $86 million. According to the plant's most recent annual report, the facility produces 42 million liters of fresh water per day, enough to supply roughly a third of the city's demand, and operations are overseen by chief engineer Dr. Amara Okonkwo. In June 2023 the plant suffered a membrane fouling incident that cut output by 60 percent. Investigators attributed the fouling to an algal bloom offshore, and the bloom itself was traced to fertilizer runoff from farms in the Kessler Valley. Repairs took eleven days and cost $2.4 million. In response, the plant installed an ultraviolet pretreatment stage, a change that reduced the frequency of membrane cleaning from weekly to monthly. Citing the disruption, the city council approved construction of a second desalination plant, which is scheduled to open in 2027.

SUMMARY:
Port Merrow's Halvorsen Desalination Plant, opened in March 2019 for $86 million, produces 42 million liters daily - about a third of city demand. A June 2023 algal-bloom fouling incident, traced to Kessler Valley fertilizer runoff, cut output 60 percent; repairs took eleven days and cost $2.4 million.
